| [LIT-002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-002.md) v2 | Nested Hierarchical Dirichlet Processes | Paisley et al. (2012), [ARXIV-1210.6738](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.6738). The nHDP gives each document its own DP over the children of every node of a shared global nCRP tree (G_i^(d) ~ DP(βG_i)), plus a per-node stop/continue switch U_{d,i} ~ Beta(γ1, γ2). Each word then takes its own path, and β → 0 recovers the single-path nCRP. The paper fits this with SVI plus a greedy per-document subtree selection. On small corpora the variational nHDP beats variational nCRP on all three datasets and Gibbs nCRP on two of three (PNAS −6.304 vs −6.496/−6.574 held-out log-likelihood). On 1.8M NYT and 2.7M Wikipedia documents it tops stochastic HDP and LDA-50/150/250 by roughly 0.08 and 0.11 nats (read off Figs. 2, 7), using ≈12 and ≈8 topics per document. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-023); the reference construction of the nHDP and a compact worked example of conjugate-exponential SVI for a tree-structured nonparametric model. Two things about it: the global update equations (23, 26–27) as printed contradict the paper's own §4.1.2 derivation, and the large-scale results never compare against the nCRP. |
| [LIT-003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-003.md) v2 | A structure theorem for generalized-noncontextual ontological models | Schmid et al. Then M(T) = χ_B ∘ T ∘ χ_A⁻¹ for unique invertible linear maps χ_A (Thm 4.1). Consequences: - Every diagram-preserving quasiprobabilistic model is an exact (non-overcomplete) frame representation (Prop. 4.3). - Every diagram-preserving noncontextual ontological model has \|Λ_A\| = dim(A), the GPT dimension (Cor. 4.2, §4.3): exactly d² ontic states for a qudit and 4 for a qubit. - The paper also proves (Cor. 3.5) that three things are equivalent in arbitrary compositional scenarios, without needing tomographic locality: a noncontextual ontological model of the operational theory; an ontological model (simplex embedding) of its GPT; and a positive quasiprobabilistic model of its GPT. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-017); It is the formal backbone of the "classicality = generalized noncontextuality = positive quasiprobability" position that LIT-007 and LIT-019 appeal to. Remedies opinion after the 2024 §2 liability ruling. "Qualified Competitors" is rewritten so it can include GenAI firms. The term is six years (five plus one of ramp-up). On GenAI, the court finds that grounded chatbots perform an information-retrieval function similar to general search engines, enough to bring GenAI inside the decree. | [LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md) v2 | Quasi-quantization: classical statistical theories with an epistemic restriction | Spekkens (2014), [ARXIV-1409.5041](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.5041). Take a classical statistical theory over a phase space Ω = R^{2n} or (Z_d)^{2n}, and allow only uniform distributions over V^⊥ + v, where V is an isotropic subspace (a Poisson-commuting set of linear "quadrature" variables) and v ∈ V gives their values. The result is operationally identical to the quadrature quantum subtheory (the stabilizer formalism for odd prime d) for continuous variables and for odd prime d; the proof is that the Wigner functions of that subtheory are exactly these distributions (§IV.A). For d = 2 the two theories are isomorphic element by element but make different predictions, because the qubit stabilizer subtheory is contextual (§IV.B). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-013); the clearest single statement of the epistricted-theory programme, and the source of the weak/strong nonclassicality split that 2111.13727 and 2005.07161 build on; read it for §II–IV and App. A, not for Table II, which it asserts rather than derives. |

| [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md) v3 | Distinguishability and Accessible Information in Quantum Theory | Fuchs (1995), [arXiv:quant-ph/9601020](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9601020). Minimizing the Bhattacharyya overlap Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) over all POVMs gives exactly F(ρ0,ρ1) = tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28). The minimum is attained by a projective measurement in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67). For binary ensembles, the same Schwarz-inequality technique gives three results: a short proof of the Holevo bound I(t) ≤ S(t), with equality iff [ρ0,ρ1] = 0 (Eq. 3.149); a tighter upper bound L(t) (Eq. 3.187, integrated in Eqs. 3.230/3.244; closed form for qubits in Eq. 3.269); and a measurement-attained lower bound M(t) = tr[(1−t)ρ0 ln L_ρ(ρ0) + tρ1 ln L_ρ(ρ1)] (Eq. 3.203). | [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md) v2 | Why interference phenomena do not capture the essence of quantum theory | Catani et al. (2021), [ARXIV-2111.13727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13727). The paper models each mode of the interferometer as a classical bit pair (occupation N ∈ Z_2, phase Φ ∈ Z_2). The agent may know only one of N, Φ or N⊕Φ and must be maximally ignorant of the rest. Under that restriction, local and deterministic dynamics (beamsplitter: swap N_L with Φ_L⊕Φ_R) reproduce exactly the 50-50, ϕ ∈ {0, π} Mach–Zehnder statistics (output port L with probability 1 or 0; ½/½ with a which-way detector). The same holds for the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb tester (success probability ¼), delayed choice and the quantum eraser (interference within each P_A outcome class, none within each Q_A class). So this "TRAP" slice of interference phenomenology cannot, on its own, force wave–particle complementarity, observer-dependence or nonlocal/retrocausal influence. The paper leaves aside the phenomenology it concedes is nonclassical (unbalanced beamsplitters, the functional form of the duality relation, Hardy's interferometer). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-018); It is the worked, experiment-by-experiment defence of placing interference in the weakly nonclassical column of LIT-007's Table II, and it has the clearest statement of the Spekkens-school methodology (define classicality, formalize it, prove a no-go). Read §3, §4.3, §5.1 and App. A. Its noncontextuality claim for the toy field theory is asserted, not proved. |

An editorial review with no new result. Its one formal item (§4, Eq. 4.1: x(t+1) = f[x(t)], x(0) = x₀) sorts phenomena three ways. Non-emergent: local rules plus initial conditions let you deduce the "expected" high-level pattern. Weakly emergent: they let you deduce an "unexpected" one by computation. Strongly emergent: no deduction is possible even in principle. "Unexpected" is never defined. The rest is a cross-domain survey (§3), a 16-paper map of the theme issue (§5), and an outlook (§6). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-007); worth reading as the table of contents and framing of the Phil. If N entities' resources follow GBM (drift μ, volatility σ, independent noise), then pooling and sharing equally every step leaves the drift at μ, cuts the volatility to σ/√N (Eq. 3.9), and raises each member's time-average growth rate from μ − σ²/2 to μ − σ²/(2N) (Eq. 4.1). The premium is (σ²/2)(1 − 1/N) (Eq. 4.2). The homogeneous state is unstable exactly when the species are self-attracting, μ(p) − μ(s) < 0 (Eq. 6). The paper argues philosophically, not formally, that the quantum theory of open systems "GT" is more fundamental than standard closed-system quantum theory "ST". GT treats states as density operators that evolve, in general, non-unitarily, and it admits not-completely-positive maps. The ontic and epistemic cases each win only on a second, interpretation- or practice-laden criterion: OntFund-2 and EpFund-2. On the first, formal criteria (OntFund-1, EpFund-1) the two frameworks tie, and the authors say so because Stinespring dilation and dropping the Lindblad terms translate in both directions (§4.1, §4.2.1). Explanatory fundamentality is granted only deflationarily (ExFund-1), and the authors recommend dropping the notion (§4.2.2). The step from there to "the open systems view is fundamental tout court" (§4.3) rests on the special sciences and on "there are no other options". | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-077); worth reading as the clearest statement of the "open systems view" and of the distinction between a view, a framework, a theory and a model (§2, §4.1, §5.2). It defines the environment's work capacity C_work = max over agent models of ⟨H(A_t\|M_t) − H(S_t\|M_t)⟩_t (in k_BT ln 2 per round) and proves two things. First, for unifilar environments whose percepts ignore actions, the efficient agents are exactly the randomize-and-forget ∩ maximally-predictive ones, and C_work = log\|A\| − h(S). | [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md) v2 | Shannon invariants: A scalable approach to information decomposition | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2504.15779](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15779). For any set of quantities Π(α) satisfying the PID consistency equation (A7), whatever the redundancy measure, two averages are fixed by Shannon quantities alone. They are the average degree of redundancy, r̄ = Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) (Prop. 1), and the average degree of vulnerability, v̄ = Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y) (Prop. 2). Two identities follow: RSI = (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y) (Cor. 1), and a new "dual" index DRSI = I(X;Y) − Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ) = (1 − v̄)·I(X;Y) (Prop. 4, Cor. 2). In small, stochastically quantised (8-level) networks analysed on their own training set, r̄ about the label rises with depth and v̄ falls with depth and training. In a face autoencoder, decoder layers are more redundant than size-matched encoder layers, and r̄ rises with bottleneck width. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-045); the theory (§II–III, App. B) is short, correct and redundancy-measure-free. | [LIT-044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md) v2 | The Epic Story of Maximum Likelihood | Stigler (2007), [ARXIV-0804.2996](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.2996). Stigler gives a history of maximum likelihood from Lagrange (1769) to Le Cam (1953). Fisher gave three optimality arguments. The 1922 one rests on the false belief that ML estimates are always sufficient. The 1925 "ANOVA" one derives the information inequality V ≥ 1/I(θ) from Var X = E Var(X\|T) + Var E(X\|T), treating approximate normality as exact. The third, sent privately to Hotelling in 1930, holds for multinomial models and smooth degree-0-homogeneous estimators, and was published only in disguise in 1935. Stigler's verdict is that the Neyman–Scott growing-parameter example (Wald 1938, published 1948) is the practically important failure. He calls Hodges's 1951 superefficiency example "an ingenious but minor technical achievement", because the superefficiency set has Lebesgue measure zero (Le Cam 1953). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-074); an authoritative, archive-based history by the leading historian of statistics, and worth reading for exactly which ML optimality claims were proved, under what conditions, and which counterexamples matter. It is a history, not a technical reference: for modern conditions it points to Bahadur (1964), Le Cam (1953, 1990), van der Vaart (1998) and Cox (2006). |
| [LIT-045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md) v5 | Structural Realism | Ladyman (2007), <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/structural-realism/>. The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the lesson of theory change. What is retained, and what we are entitled to believe, is structure, understood by ontic structuralists as modal structure. It sorts the view into an epistemic form, which falls to the Newman/Demopoulos–Friedman triviality result when stated as a Ramsey sentence (§3.2), and an ontic form with seven distinguishable theses, from eliminativism about individuals to "objects are constructs" (§4). The ontic form is motivated by quantum non-individuality and entanglement, gauge symmetry and the hole argument. The entry closes with seven objections, each answered in the author's own voice (§5). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md)); the standard map of the structural-realism literature, written by the founder of OSR. For finite-state chains the ordinary plug-in estimator is exactly this estimator, with d = (a−1)a^k(b^k−1). For a linear Gaussian VAR, T̂ is half the Granger-causality statistic. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-053); a short, correct letter and the standard citation for reading transfer entropy as a log-likelihood ratio. | [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) v2 | The Homological Nature of Entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), DOI-10.3390/e17053253. On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. The information cohomology H*(S;Q) is computed by a Hochschild-type bar complex whose action is Shannon's averaged conditioning. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. In the unitary-invariant quantum case H¹_U = 0: Shannon entropy is the coboundary of minus the von Neumann entropy, which is the unique invariant 0-cochain with that property up to an additive constant (Thm 3). The tree ("arborescent") version again gives H¹ spanned by entropy (Thm 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md)); the founding paper of information cohomology, with complete proofs of the degree-one results (Thms 1, 3, 4). Reduction elsewhere moves away from a point of view toward the objective; here that move leads away from the thing being explained. So physicalism may be true, but we have no conception of how it could be. He then argues that ψ describes random discontinuous motion (RDM) of N point particles in 3-space: \|ψ\|² is the density with which each particle is present at each instant, and ψ is a single-case propensity. For theories with ideal existence, uniqueness and a dynamical time-translation group, time is three intertwined ℝ-actions (on spacetime, on the symplectic space of solutions, and on the isomorphic space of initial data), and change is a slicing-indexed family of functions on those spaces. Singular dynamics, gauge freedom and time-dependence each damage this picture in a repairable way. Spatially compact vacuum GR breaks it, because the reduced Hamiltonian vanishes (h ≡ 0) and there is only one canonical isomorphism between the reduced spaces. That is the problem of time. It is not an artefact of the 3+1 split, it does not show change to be illusory, and it is absent from asymptotically flat GR and from artificially generally covariant theories. A parameterized "geometric time", such as CMC, restores change and, in the CMC case, a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-118.md)); worth reading as the careful technical-philosophical statement of what the problem of time is and is not in classical GR. Hempel's "inductive risk" (the chance of wrongly accepting or rejecting a hypothesis) arises at three internal stages of science: choosing a methodology such as a significance level, characterising data, and interpreting results. Wherever the non-epistemic consequences of error can be foreseen, weighing them requires non-epistemic values. Douglas shows this on dioxin cancer studies. Three pathologist panels (1978, 1980, 1990) scored the same Kociba rat-liver slides differently (e.g. 34/50, 33/47, 18/50 tumours at 100 ng/kg/day). The chapter argues by analogy that deep neural networks are "stochastic measuring devices". The trained weights are a model, and generation is simulation. DNNs are stochastic because random initialisation and non-convex loss mean runs need not converge to the same weights, failing Baird's "regularity" condition. The problems of interpreting model states and generated text are therefore the familiar problems of instruments, models and simulations. The paper proposes a definition, (MSC). A mathematical structure S = ((A_i), (S_j)) is a structure *of* conscious experience iff (S1) its domains are sets of experiential aspects, and (S2) every relation or function S_j has an "S_j-aspect". An S_j-aspect is an aspect that a variation of experience changes exactly when the variation fails to preserve S_j. The older condition (MDC), that a structure is "of" experience if its domains are aspects and its axioms hold, survives only as the necessary condition for *describing* experience, because as a sufficient condition it admits incompatible structures (discrete and non-discrete topologies on the same set), arbitrary re-definitions (every C·d for C > 0) and consciousness-indifferent structures. Lossless compression of trained-model files works almost entirely through the float exponent. It is concentrated on about 40 of 256 values, the top 12 hold ~99.9% of parameters, and it compresses to ~33% under order-0 Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa stay ≈100%. So "regular" BF16 models compress to ~66.4% and FP32 models to ~83%. Rounded "clean" models reach 33.7–48.1%, and ZipNN (exponent extraction plus Huffman only) beats vanilla Zstd by 17% in size and 62% in single-thread speed on Llama-3.1-8B BF16. That export need not take the form of heat (p. 1). Logically reversible operations, including copying onto a blank register and measurement, have no minimum cost.
